source: Chalkidis, Jana, Hartung, Bommarito, Androutsopoulos, Katz, Aletras. LexGLUE: A Benchmark Dataset for Legal Language Understanding in English. ACL 2022, pp. 4310-4330. arXiv:2110.00976v4 (8 Nov 2022), Table 3 (test) and Tables 5-6 (development).
task: SCOTUS, multi-class issue-area classification, 5,000/1,400/1,400 train/dev/test; the paper's dataset table lists 14 classes (13 occur in the released splits)

protocol.bert_family_input: hierarchical variant: each of up to 64 paragraphs of 128 tokens encoded independently, 2-layer transformer over paragraph [CLS] vectors, max-pool, linear + softmax
protocol.longformer_bigbird_input: up to 4096 tokens, default sparse-attention settings
protocol.optimizer: Adam, initial learning rate 3e-5, up to 20 epochs, early stopping on development data, fp16, batch size 8
protocol.seeds_and_reporting: five seeds; Table 3 reports the TEST score of the single seed with the best DEVELOPMENT score (not a five-seed mean)

appendix_d: Hierarchical BERT (64x128) outperforms standard 512-token BERT on SCOTUS by 4.9 percentage points.
comparability_notes: LexGLUE reports a best-development-seed test score; this study reports five-seed means and per-seed values.
Different optimiser settings (Adam 3e-5, batch 8, 20 epochs) from this study's matched protocol (AdamW 2e-5, batch 16, 10 epochs, patience 3).
LexGLUE hierarchical models segment by paragraphs; this study's hierarchical reference splits each document into consecutive 126-token chunks (+[CLS]/[SEP]).
Values are quoted for context only and are not treated as directly comparable.
